### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a931063df36e283a25ef618885c919e53a096846` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4ed448b22f9a0f867971f2213f1b6f2c2fe332dd` — the merge of head `21e33be20323b6475f4fe2058acc30cc60d80fff` into base `a931063df36e283a25ef618885c919e53a096846`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4ed448b22f9a0f867971f2213f1b6f2c2fe332dd && git checkout 4ed448b22f9a0f867971f2213f1b6f2c2fe332dd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a931063df36e283a25ef618885c919e53a096846 21e33be20323b6475f4fe2058acc30cc60d80fff && git checkout -B drift-repro a931063df36e283a25ef618885c919e53a096846 && git merge --no-ff 21e33be20323b6475f4fe2058acc30cc60d80fff

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a931063df36e283a25ef618885c919e53a096846
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对

**L1 first review: ACCEPT** · PR #34712 · card #34636 · area o2-A · L1-a2 · 2026-11-17T08:39Z

Head-sha: `21e33be20323b6475f4fe2058acc30cc60d80fff`

Final-head comment 6943024021; dev report 6942160729; flake note 6942531202.

### Checklist

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`. `Fixes #34636` is the only closing keyword in the body. It is right: the PR delivers all three of the card's Acceptance boxes.
  - `Clause-②: no` holds. Both rules stay advisories (a suggestion and a warning), and nothing an author writes is refused.
  - `Metadata-protocol: none` holds as well.
- **Scope** (`get_files`, 3 paths, +104/−4): `packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts`, a new test file, and the changeset. The commits are `b125220c` and merge `21e33be2`, whose `git show --remerge-diff` is empty.
- **The predicate.** `isInlineEdited(def)` is file-local and not exported. It returns true for `true`, `'grid'` and `'form'`, which are exactly the three values `isBodyTableRelationship` (`related-list-body-table.ts:59`) treats as inline-edited.
  - The card asked to call the spec predicate if possible. The body explains why it does not, and I checked the reason at `related-list-body-table.ts:54-60`. `isBodyTableRelationship` returns `false` for any type other than `master_detail` (it also admits `lookup` only through `relatedList: 'primary'`), and it answers `relatedList` first. Reusing it would change R5's and R6's reach, so a local predicate for the narrower question is the right call.
  - All three sites in the file now use it: R5, R6, and the `inline-edit-needs-bulk` loop (`:316`). The loop previously spelled out the same three values, so its behaviour does not change.
- **R5** (`relationship/line-items-inline-edit`, `:1164`). It is now silent for all three values and nudges only on absent or `false`. The rule id, severity, message and fix are unchanged. A `'grid'` / `'form'` author is no longer offered a fix that would overwrite their chosen mode.
- **R6** (`relationship/association-inline-edit`, `:1188`). It now warns for all three values, not just `true`. That is the card's second box.
- **Pins.** 10 cases: R5 silent on each of the three values, R5 nudging on `undefined` and `false`, R6 warning on each of the three values, and R6 silent on `undefined` and `false`.
  - **Premise.** On unmodified `main` source, 4 fail (the `'grid'` / `'form'` legs of both rules).
  - **Ablations** (body). Reverting R5's condition turns its `'grid'` and `'form'` legs red (2 failed / 8 passed). Reverting R6's condition does the same for R6. Both were restored to `blob == HEAD` (`78bd1208`). The `true` legs and the absent/`false` legs stay green under each ablation, so they act as the controls.
- **Customer-facing text.** `skills/objectstack-data/references/lint-rules.md:15,18` describe the two rules as "without `inlineEdit`" and "marked `inlineEdit`". That wording does not name a value, so it was already true of all three modes and is now matched by the code. No `Skills-docs:` line is owed. No other surface states the rules' trigger.
- **Changeset** (root `.changeset/`, `@objectstack/lint` patch). I checked each sentence against the diff: the three accepted values, R5 silent for any of them, R6 now warning on `'grid'` and `'form'`, and ids, severities and messages unchanged. They match.
- **Gates.** 63 derived, 63 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. The lint package suite reads 215 files / 9117 passed, with typecheck exit 0.

### CI on this head

- **check-runs, `filter=latest`, 70 runs:** `success=57`, `skipped=13`, nothing red or pending.
- **Flake judgement: accepted.** `Test Core (4/8)` went red on the first run on one case, `validate-expressions.flow-null-guards.test.ts:457`, timed out at 5230 ms against the 5000 ms limit. The flake note 6942531202 reads it as timing.
  - That case does run every lint rule through `os build`, so it does pass through this file. But the added predicate is three strict-equality checks, and nothing in the diff could cost 230 ms.
  - A single re-run of the job is `success` (08:36:56Z), and that is the latest run.

### L2 and landing

- **L2: not owed.** Nothing under `packages/spec/src/**`, `Clause-②: no`, no narrowing (an advisory that fires on more values refuses nothing), and no governed rule text.
- **Landing tier** (`node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34712`): `NOT governed — ordinary queue landing`, 108 changed lines ≤ 3000. This is not spec surface. The area lands it, and no human approval is needed.
